paragraphs: Trucks and trailers are bought and matched separately in the real world, and a collection that supplies both lets a scene do the same: a tractor unit with a curtainsider, the same unit with a tanker, a different cab with a flatbed. That interchange is what makes a yard or a motorway look like a working fleet.

Supplying them together also keeps coupling heights and scale consistent, which is the detail that goes wrong when a tractor and a trailer come from different sources and the fifth wheel does not line up.

Two more collections sit on this page at $299 and $499 for wider selections. This set at $278 is aimed at logistics and supply chain visualisation, highway and depot scenes, fleet marketing, film and television, and games. Built to CheckMate specification, on sale since 2026.

An ocean research ship is a laboratory with a hull: an A frame over the stern for launching equipment, cranes along the working deck, a moon pool in some designs and accommodation for scientists as well as crew. Adding a helicopter on the aft deck shows the vessel operating rather than moored.
The mesh runs 447,918 polygons and 471,407 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the ship, the deck equipment and the aircraft.

At $269 and built to StemCell specification, it suits oceanographic and scientific visualisation, marine research and expedition presentation, documentary and news graphics, offshore industry material and games. On sale since 2025.

Loading is where a transport aircraft makes sense: ramp down, forklift driving a pallet up into the hold, and the whole airframe suddenly reading as a piece of logistics rather than as an aeroplane. This build stages that moment, with the aircraft, the ramp, the forklift and the load together.
The mesh runs 540,642 polygons and 568,569 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and it arrives rigged so the forks lift and the aircraft ramp can be positioned.

At $269 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits defence logistics visualisation, military aviation presentation, humanitarian and airlift material, documentary graphics, training content and games. On sale since 2025.

A helicopter carrier is a flat top without a catapult, and the deck layout follows from that: landing spots marked along the length, a starboard island, and lifts sized for rotorcraft rather than for jets. Adding a heavy tandem rotor helicopter on deck gives the scale immediately.
The mesh runs 2,049,448 polygons and 2,149,209 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the deck markings, the island and the aircraft.

This page carries four other builds from $199 to $269, including the ship alone, in dry dock and with different aircraft. Aimed at naval and defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, museum material, film and television, and games. Built to CheckMate specification, on sale since 2025.

A lorry loader is operated from the ground beside the vehicle, not from a cab, which is why the controls are on a stand at the base of the column and why the operator is part of any honest picture of the machine working. This build includes that figure along with the truck and the boom.
The mesh runs 599,278 polygons and 647,872 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the chassis, the crane, the outriggers and the operator.

At $269 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits construction and logistics visualisation, equipment marketing and catalogues, site safety and training material, delivery scenes and games. On sale since 2025.

The amphitheatre survives as a ruin with one side largely intact and the other stripped back, which means an accurate model has to be asymmetric. That contrast between the standing arcades and the exposed inner structure is the whole image, and a complete reconstruction would be a different building entirely.

The mesh runs 1,419,065 polygons and 1,358,423 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, and ships with 30 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the travertine, the weathering and the missing stone.

At $259 it suits travel and tourism material, heritage and archaeological visualisation, city and landmark renders, documentary and education content, film and television, and games. On sale since 2019.

Two seated figures on a bench is one of the most useful groupings in architectural visualisation and one of the least often available: most people libraries supply walkers and shoppers, not people who have stopped. The posture is different too - settled, leaning, turned slightly toward each other.
The mesh is efficient at 74,228 polygons and 83,312 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits figures placed in a wider scene rather than examined closely.

At $249 and built to StemCell specification, it suits architectural and urban visualisation, healthcare and social care material, community and public space presentation, editorial imagery and games. On sale since 2025.

A sectioned eye is how the organ gets taught, because almost everything important is inside: the lens behind the iris, the vitreous filling the globe, the retina lining the back and the optic nerve leaving it. A whole eye shows a sphere; a cut one shows an optical instrument.

The mesh runs 212,864 polygons and 214,566 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 45 texture maps - 40 at 4096x4096 and 5 at 2048x2048, which is what the retinal vasculature and the iris detail demand.

At $249 and built to StemCell specification, it suits ophthalmology and optometry education, medical and patient communication, courseware and textbook illustration, device marketing and broadcast medical work. On sale since 2020.

This stadium is a full bowl rather than four separate stands, with a continuous ring of seating and a roof that reaches out over most of it. That continuity is the defining feature and the hardest part to model, because the geometry has to sweep without a break the whole way round.

It is a very large asset at 5,166,602 polygons and 6,360,389 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, and ships with 41 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096. Every seat is geometry, which is why the bowl holds up from the pitch as well as from the air.
At $249 it suits sports broadcast graphics, venue and architectural visualisation, tourism and city material, football games and print. On sale since 2016.

The high mobility vehicle exists in an unusual number of variants: troop carrier, weapons carrier, ambulance, shelter carrier, each on the same chassis with a completely different back end. A convoy needs that variety, and one body style repeated immediately reads as a game asset rather than a unit.
Supplying the variants as a collection keeps the chassis, the ride height and the finish consistent between them, which is exactly what breaks when vehicles are assembled from separate purchases.
At $249 it suits defence and military visualisation, documentary and news graphics, film and television, training material and games. On sale since 2018.

A powership is a power station built on a hull, moored at a port and connected to a national grid by cable. That gives it a deck covered in generator halls, exhaust stacks and switchgear rather than in cargo gear, and it explains why the superstructure looks industrial rather than nautical.
The mesh runs 2,232,979 polygons and 2,494,063 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the generator housings, the stacks and the deck equipment.

An unladen tanker sits on this page at $149. The powership at $249 suits energy and infrastructure visualisation, maritime industry presentation, developing markets and utility material, documentary graphics and games. Built to StemCell specification, on sale since 2023.

A bucket wheel excavator is among the largest land vehicles ever built, and its scale is impossible to convey without something beside it. Pairing it with a mining truck, itself enormous, is the standard way of showing that - and this build supplies both so the comparison is built in.
It is a very large asset at 4,378,344 polygons and 2,288,165 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the wheel, the boom lattice and the conveyor structure.

This page carries rigged builds from $299 to $359, including versions prepared for Maya and Cinema 4D. Aimed at mining and heavy industry visualisation, equipment marketing, documentary work, engineering presentation and games. On sale since 2022.

A semi submersible floats on submerged pontoons rather than standing on the seabed, which is what lets it work in water far too deep for a jack up. The columns connecting the pontoons to the deck are the visible signature, and they are why the structure looks like a platform on legs standing in nothing.

The mesh runs 4,071,096 polygons and 4,154,300 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 41 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the rust, the salt staining and the repainted plating.

A rigged build sits on this page at $299. The static model at $249 covers offshore energy visualisation, oil and gas marketing, maritime and engineering presentation, documentary work and games. On sale since 2018.

A bipedal walk is the hardest thing to animate convincingly and the single thing that makes a humanoid robot believable. Getting the weight transfer, the slight sway and the pause at each step right is a specialist job, and this build arrives with a slow walk cycle already animated.
It is rigged and prepared for Maya, so the cycle can be retimed, looped or blended into other motion in the application it was built for rather than being rebuilt from a static mesh.

At $239 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits robotics and automation marketing, future of work and technology presentation, technology journalism, previsualisation and games. On sale since 2026.
